Identity.History: Cash crops in the ancient world were agricultural products grown primarily for sale, taxation, or export rather than direct household consumption. Common examples included olives and olive oil, grapes and wine, flax for linen, dates, spices, and other regionally valuable commodities. Their cultivation tied rural estates to wider trade networks and could generate substantial wealth for landowners, merchants, temples, and states, especially in areas able to specialize in products sought by distant markets.
Identity.Tooltip: Build in neutral or own territory to harvest cash crops for coin. Build around a Farmstead to gain a +100% farming boost. There is a diminishing return effect where it is more efficient to use fewer gatherers per field. Max gatherers: 5.
